Since we are selecting exactly 1 task, there are no dependency edges, but the task itself is well-suited for a benchmark: the block has a distinctive visual appearance (purple translucent glass) making it observable, and the scene can be designed with interesting navigation challenges to reach it.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate/observe task. The player must navigate near the stone brick chapel and face the purple stained glass windows. Target is set to the center of the glass cluster at spawn-relative [7, 2, 7], with max_distance=5 (player must be within 5 blocks) and facing_tolerance=60 degrees (player must be looking toward the glass). This models 'player can see the purple stained glass' without requiring them to stand on an exact spot.

scene_description: A small stone brick chapel/building with purple stained glass windows on all four walls, located ~6-8 blocks east and ~5-8 blocks south of spawn. An oak planks shed sits to the northwest at ~-3,-1 to ~-1,-3. A cobblestone path connects the spawn area to the chapel. The player must navigate to the chapel and find the purple stained glass windows.
task_text: Find the purple stained glass blocks. Look around the area, locate the stone brick building with purple stained glass windows, and approach it.
design_notes: The stone brick chapel is at ~5,0,5 to ~8,4,8 (4x4 footprint). Purple stained glass windows are placed at y=2 on all four walls, with extra glass at y=3 on the north face. The interior is hollowed out (2x2x3 air). An open oak door on the west face at ~5,1-2,7. A cobblestone path from ~0,0,2 to ~3,0,5 guides the player toward the building. An oak planks shed at ~-3,0,-3 to ~-1,3,-1 serves as a minor distraction. Note: command 17 (oak_door upper) overwrites the purple_stained_glass at ~5,2,7 — this is intentional as the door takes priority there. The purple glass is still present on 9 other positions.
